about: Synthetic planner cases for the orchestrated Debrief (no production data). Each case is a session whose right planner choice is known by construction: the profile and the Analyst's evidence summary carry exactly the signal an agent's use_when names. Used today by ally-ai tests/core/debrief_graph/test_orchestrator_fixtures.py (planner wiring with a fake model) and ally-be src/debrief/test/debrief-orchestrator-metrics.spec.ts (metric rollups); an offline planner eval can load the same file later. `expected.choose` = agents a good plan includes; `expected.never` = agents it must not include (many are simply not offered); `expected.offered` / `expected.notOffered` = what code must and must not show the planner; `expectedFindings` = what protocol_check should find (quotes are exact transcript words, checked by the quote verifier).

protocols.title: Refer when low mood lasts two weeks
protocols.text: If a caller describes low mood on most days for two weeks or longer, suggest they see a GP or a counsellor, and offer the referral list before the call ends.

protocols.title: Give the helpline on any self-harm mention
protocols.text: Whenever a caller mentions self-harm, give the 24-hour crisis helpline number and ask whether they can keep themselves safe tonight.

cases.about: The organisation has two protocols and the client mentions self-harm; the trainee moves on to coping tips without the helpline.

transcript.text: Hi, thanks for calling. What's on your mind tonight?
Work has been awful and I can't sleep.
That sounds exhausting. How long has it been like this?
A while. Last night I thought about cutting myself again.
Have you tried a warm bath before bed? Some people find that helps.
I guess I could try that.
Great, let's talk about a sleep routine.

behaviours.quote: Have you tried a warm bath before bed?
behaviours.note: Moved to tips after a self-harm disclosure.

pivotal_moments.summary: Client discloses recent thoughts of self-harm and the trainee moves straight to sleep tips
pivotal_moments.why_it_matters: A risk disclosure needs safety questions first.

protocol_check.quote: Have you tried a warm bath before bed?
protocol_check.point: The organisation's protocol says to give the crisis helpline when self-harm is mentioned; the trainee moved on to sleep tips instead.

cases.about: No risk cue, but the client describes a month of low mood and the trainee never suggests a referral: the low-mood protocol applies.

transcript.text: Hello, how are you doing today?
Honestly I've felt low pretty much every day for about a month.
A month is a long time to feel that way.
Yeah. I just drag myself through the day.
What keeps you going on the hard days?
My dog, mostly.
It sounds like your dog matters a lot. Thanks for sharing today.

behaviours.quote: A month is a long time to feel that way.

behaviours.note: Closed the call without suggesting further support.

pivotal_moments.summary: Client describes low mood on most days for about a month
pivotal_moments.why_it_matters: Long-lasting low mood calls for a referral.

pivotal_moments.summary: Trainee closes the call without suggesting any further support

protocol_check.point: The organisation asks for a referral when low mood lasts two weeks or more; the call closed without one.

protocol_check.quote: A month is a long time to feel that way.
protocol_check.point: The trainee picked up how long the low mood had lasted, which is what the protocol turns on.

cases.about: Four past debriefs, three of which asked the learner to work on reflecting feelings, and this session missed it again.

past_work_on_this.point: Name the feeling you hear before asking the next question.
Reflect the feeling, not only the facts.
Slow down and say back what the client feels.
Leave space after a hard disclosure.

transcript.text: What would you like to talk about?
My sister stopped speaking to me and it really hurts.
When did she stop speaking to you?
Three weeks ago, after an argument about our mum.
What was the argument about?
Who should look after her.
Have you tried calling her?

behaviours.quote: What would you like to talk about?
behaviours.note: Opened openly, then switched to fact questions.
The client named hurt twice; it was never reflected.

pivotal_moments.summary: Client says a family rift really hurts and the trainee asks for dates instead of the feeling
pivotal_moments.why_it_matters: The feeling was the door into the conversation.

cases.about: A Hindi session in which the learner writes romanised Hindi mixed with English (Latin script): the quotes are not in the debrief language's script.

transcript.text: Namaste, aaj aap kaisa feel kar rahe ho?
Bas thoda pareshan hoon, exams aa rahe hain.
Exams ka pressure bahut heavy lagta hai, haan?
Haan, raat ko neend nahi aati.
Neend na aana, that must be really tiring. Take your time.
Thank you, accha laga baat karke.
Kabhi bhi baat karni ho toh call karna.

behaviours.quote: Exams ka pressure bahut heavy lagta hai, haan?
behaviours.note: Reflected the pressure in the client's own mix.

behaviours.quote: Neend na aana, that must be really tiring.

pivotal_moments.summary: Client mentions sleeplessness before exams and the trainee acknowledges it in mixed Hindi and English
pivotal_moments.why_it_matters: The warmth rests on the language mix.

ai_faults.note: The AI client wrapped up abruptly with "accha laga" before the trainee could explore.

cases.about: An English session in which the learner writes Hindi in Devanagari alongside English: code-mixed, and a script other than the debrief language's.

transcript.text: Hello, आप कैसे हैं? What brings you here?
I've been feeling lonely since I moved cities.
नए शहर में अकेलापन, that sounds hard.
It is. I don't know anyone.
What has helped you meet people before?
Maybe joining a club.
अच्छा idea है. Let's think about which one.

behaviours.quote: नए शहर में अकेलापन, that sounds hard.
What has helped you meet people before?

pivotal_moments.summary: Trainee reflects the client's loneliness, switching between Hindi and English
pivotal_moments.why_it_matters: The switch may carry warmth the debrief should keep.

cases.about: No organisation protocols, a first session, English throughout: none of protocol_check, history_deep or language_specialist is worth running (none is even offered).

transcript.text: Hi, I'm here to listen. What's been happening?
I failed my driving test again.
That's disappointing. How are you feeling about it?
Embarrassed, mostly.
Embarrassed. Tell me more about that.
Everyone else passed first time.
It can feel like everyone else finds it easy.

behaviours.quote: Embarrassed. Tell me more about that.
behaviours.note: Named the feeling and invited more.

pivotal_moments.summary: Client names embarrassment and the trainee reflects it back
pivotal_moments.why_it_matters: A clean example of reflecting a feeling.
